items.title: Hal Galper interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 27, 2022
items.q: He picked Michael Brecker’s solo on my recording of “Triple Play” with my quintet.

ctx.x: Yeah. But I have a theory about how musical growth occurs. That’s what it was. Because when you listen to somebody the assumption has been that you’re trying to learn something from that musician. If you’re attracted to a musician that’s because I feel like you have to learn there’s something about that musician that is attracting you to him. So I have a belief that you’re born with neutral — a whole bunch of neutral neurological neurons waiting to be stimulated from the environment. It’s a thing of like the…

right? He went to the festival, he came back, he said, “Well I didn’t win.” I said, “Well play something for me.” You know. When he played he had everything I had been trying to get out of him for years. So how did that happen? Why did he pick Michael Brecker? Because Michael Brecker set off a particular neural neuron, right, that led him to pick Michael Brecker. Because that’s what he needed at that moment was to copy Michael Brecker and learn how to play with that level of intensity. Because he came back from…
